title: A Reduction of Imitation Learning and Structured Prediction to No-Regret Online Learning
relevance: Gives O(T^2 eps) compounding-error bound for supervised imitation and linear-in-T bound for DAgger; formal compounding error.

title: Breaking the Softmax Bottleneck: A High-Rank RNN Language Model
relevance: Proves the softmax bottleneck rank limit of LM output layers; formal expressivity limit of softmax LMs.

title: Theoretical Limitations of Self-Attention in Neural Sequence Models
relevance: Proves self-attention cannot model periodic or hierarchical languages without growing layers/heads; theoretical limits of attention.

title: Language Models as Knowledge Bases?
relevance: LAMA probes show relational knowledge in pretrained LMs; baseline for parametric knowledge.

title: Generalization through Memorization: Nearest Neighbor Language Models
relevance: kNN-LM interpolating a datastore helps rare patterns and factual knowledge; evidence for non-parametric memory on the tail.

title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
relevance: REALM: retrieval-augmented pretraining motivated by parametric storage needing ever-larger networks.

title: How Much Knowledge Can You Pack Into the Parameters of a Language Model?
relevance: Shows closed-book QA scales with parameters and is competitive on head facts; counterpoint on parametric knowledge.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
relevance: Original RAG model combining parametric and non-parametric memory with provenance and updatability.

title: Transformer Feed-Forward Layers Are Key-Value Memories
relevance: Shows FFN layers act as key-value memories; mechanism of parametric storage.

title: Entity-Based Knowledge Conflicts in Question Answering
relevance: Formalizes context-memory knowledge conflicts and measures over-reliance on parametric memory.

title: An Explanation of In-context Learning as Implicit Bayesian Inference
relevance: Proves ICL as implicit Bayesian inference over latent concepts under a distinguishability condition; formal lens on why distractor/stale evidence weakens in-context use.

title: Improving language models by retrieving from trillions of tokens
relevance: RETRO matches GPT-3 with 25x fewer parameters using a 2T-token database; parameter substitution by retrieval.

title: Why Exposure Bias Matters: An Imitation Learning Perspective of Error Accumulation in Language Generation
relevance: Imitation-learning analysis showing exposure bias causes error accumulation in generation.

title: Sub-Task Decomposition Enables Learning in Sequence to Sequence Tasks
relevance: Proves intermediate supervision makes composite seq2seq tasks learnable; theory for decomposition.

title: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
relevance: Shows LLM self-evaluation P(IK) is predictable and rises with relevant context; basis for abstention gating.

title: What Can Transformers Learn In-Context? A Case Study of Simple Function Classes
relevance: Shows transformers learn linear function classes in context near least squares; foundational ICL theory.

title: Atlas: Few-shot Learning with Retrieval Augmented Language Models
relevance: Atlas: retrieval-augmented 11B model beats 540B on few-shot NQ; parameter substitution by retrieval.

title: In-context Learning and Induction Heads
relevance: Identifies induction heads as a mechanism for in-context copying/learning; mechanism behind using retrieved context.

title: Large Language Models Struggle to Learn Long-Tail Knowledge
relevance: Shows QA accuracy tracks pretraining document counts and retrieval reduces dependence; empirical long-tail argument for retrieval.

title: What learning algorithm is in-context learning? Investigations with linear models
relevance: Proves transformers can implement GD and ridge regression in context and that trained ICL tracks them; ICL theory background.

title: Transformers learn in-context by gradient descent
relevance: Constructs linear self-attention equal to a gradient-descent step; mechanistic theory of in-context learning from retrieved examples.

title: When Not to Trust Language Models: Investigating Effectiveness of Parametric and Non-Parametric Memories
relevance: PopQA shows scaling fails on long-tail facts while retrieval-augmented small models beat larger ones; supports adaptive retrieval.

title: Why do Nearest Neighbor Language Models Work?
relevance: Analyzes why kNN-LMs work (representation, approximate search, softmax temperature); retrieval-augmented LM analysis.

title: In-Context Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
relevance: Shows prepending retrieved documents (In-Context RALM) gives large gains without architecture change.

title: Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
relevance: Shows irrelevant context dramatically reduces LLM reasoning accuracy; distractor effect evidence.

title: The Learnability of In-Context Learning
relevance: PAC framework showing ICL identifies rather than learns tasks; ICL learnability theory.

title: Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth: Revealing the Behavior of Large Language Models in Knowledge Conflicts
relevance: Shows LLMs accept coherent counter-memory but show confirmation bias with mixed evidence; behaviour under knowledge conflict.

title: Towards Revealing the Mystery behind Chain of Thought: A Theoretical Perspective
relevance: Proves bounded-depth transformers cannot directly solve arithmetic but can with CoT; expressivity of multi-step generation.

title: Faith and Fate: Limits of Transformers on Compositionality
relevance: Proves error probability of compositional autoregressive tasks tends to 1 exponentially with steps; supports short chains and verification.

title: What and How does In-Context Learning Learn? Bayesian Model Averaging, Parameterization, and Generalization
relevance: Proves ICL implements Bayesian model averaging with O(1/T) regret; ICL theory.

title: Birth of a Transformer: A Memory Viewpoint
relevance: Associative-memory view of transformer weights and induction head formation.

title: Memorization Capacity of Multi-Head Attention in Transformers
relevance: Bounds memorization capacity of multi-head attention in parameters; capacity theory.

title: Representational Strengths and Limitations of Transformers
relevance: Communication-complexity strengths and limits of attention (sparse averaging vs triple detection).

title: Transformers as Statisticians: Provable In-Context Learning with In-Context Algorithm Selection
relevance: Proves transformers implement many statistical algorithms and algorithm selection in context.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
relevance: Documents U-shaped position effect (lost in the middle) in multi-document QA; empirical basis for reranking and small contexts.

title: An Empirical Study of the Non-determinism of ChatGPT in Code Generation
relevance: Measures high non-determinism of ChatGPT code generation; empirical non-determinism.

title: Head-to-Tail: How Knowledgeable are Large Language Models (LLMs)? A.K.A. Will LLMs Replace Knowledge Graphs?
relevance: Head-to-Tail benchmark shows LLMs weak on torso and tail facts.

title: Language Modeling Is Compression
relevance: Establishes prediction-compression equivalence for LLMs; frames weights as a finite lossy code of the corpus versus a lossless external store.

title: The Reversal Curse: LLMs trained on "A is B" fail to learn "B is A"
relevance: Reversal curse: A-is-B training does not yield B-is-A, but in-context works; motivates bidirectional indexes.

title: Physics of Language Models: Part 3.1, Knowledge Storage and Extraction
relevance: Shows stored knowledge may be unextractable unless augmented during pretraining; argues against relying on parametric storage of rarely-seen facts.

title: Physics of Language Models: Part 3.2, Knowledge Manipulation
relevance: Shows LMs fail inverse knowledge search and comparison without CoT; motivates bidirectional indexes and alias tables in the store.

title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
relevance: Identifies attention sinks on initial tokens; positional attention phenomenon.

title: Scaling Laws for Associative Memories
relevance: Scaling laws for outer-product associative memories; capacity theory.

title: The Expressive Power of Transformers with Chain of Thought
relevance: Proves CoT with t(n) steps simulates t(n)-time Turing machines and that no-CoT transformers are in TC0; expressivity vs step count.

title: Calibrated Language Models Must Hallucinate
relevance: Proves calibrated LMs hallucinate on arbitrary facts at about the Good-Turing monofact rate and names a generation-time fact database as the mitigation; core justification for an external store.

title: Hallucination is Inevitable: An Innate Limitation of Large Language Models
relevance: Diagonalization proof that every computable LLM hallucinates, with an explicit remark that the theorem is inapplicable when external knowledge about the ground truth is retrieved.

title: The Power of Noise: Redefining Retrieval for RAG Systems
relevance: Shows high-scoring non-relevant passages hurt RAG and random passages can help; empirical RAG context-composition evidence.

title: On the Self-Verification Limitations of Large Language Models on Reasoning and Planning Tasks
relevance: Shows self-critique collapses while sound external verification helps; supports deterministic verifiers.

title: On Limitations of the Transformer Architecture
relevance: Communication-complexity proof that a transformer layer cannot compose functions over large domains; motivates doing joins in the data layer.

title: Chain of Thought Empowers Transformers to Solve Inherently Serial Problems
relevance: Proves constant-depth transformers are in AC0 without CoT and simulate size-T circuits with T CoT steps.

title: Same Task, More Tokens: the Impact of Input Length on the Reasoning Performance of Large Language Models
relevance: Shows reasoning degrades at input lengths far below context limits.

title: The pitfalls of next-token prediction
relevance: Argues teacher-forcing can fail to learn accurate next-token predictors on planning tasks; nuance on compounding-error arguments.

title: Knowledge Conflicts for LLMs: A Survey
relevance: Survey taxonomy of context-memory, inter-context and intra-memory knowledge conflicts.

title: Physics of Language Models: Part 3.3, Knowledge Capacity Scaling Laws
relevance: Measures ~2 bits of extractable knowledge per parameter with an information-theoretic bit lower bound; bounds parametric memory for enterprise facts.

title: Language Generation in the Limit
relevance: Proves language generation in the limit is possible for every countable collection; foundation for later hallucination/breadth results.

title: ClashEval: Quantifying the tug-of-war between an LLM's internal prior and external evidence
relevance: Quantifies LLMs adopting wrong retrieved content over 60% of the time, modulated by prior confidence; conflict evidence.

title: Retrieval Head Mechanistically Explains Long-Context Factuality
relevance: Finds sparse retrieval heads whose pruning causes hallucination; shows in-context retrieval runs through a narrow channel.

title: Does Fine-Tuning LLMs on New Knowledge Encourage Hallucinations?
relevance: Shows new knowledge learned via fine-tuning increases hallucination; supports an external write path for facts.

title: Certifiably Robust RAG against Retrieval Corruption
relevance: Certifiable robustness of RAG against injected passages via isolate-then-aggregate; formal poisoning defence.

title: A Theory for Token-Level Harmonization in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
relevance: Token-level theory of RAG benefit vs detriment via KL terms scaled by number of passages; formal reason stale/duplicated passages hurt.

title: Transformers need glasses! Information over-squashing in language tasks
relevance: Proves representational collapse and over-squashing in decoder-only transformers; limits on using long contexts.

title: Scaling Laws for Fact Memorization of Large Language Models
relevance: Fact memorization scales linearly with model size; memorizing all Wikidata would need ~1000B params; capacity evidence.

title: Found in the Middle: Calibrating Positional Attention Bias Improves Long Context Utilization
relevance: Links lost-in-the-middle to U-shaped intrinsic attention bias and calibrates it to improve RAG.

title: The Good, The Bad, and The Greedy: Evaluation of LLMs Should Not Ignore Non-Determinism
relevance: Shows greedy decoding generally beats sampling and evaluation must account for non-determinism.

title: Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling
relevance: Shows coverage scales with repeated sampling and becomes accuracy only with automatic verifiers.

title: Non-Determinism of "Deterministic" LLM Settings
relevance: Measures up to 15% accuracy variation in deterministic-configured LLMs; empirical non-determinism evidence.

title: A Statistical Framework for Data-dependent Retrieval-Augmented Models
relevance: Excess-risk bounds for retrieval-augmented models separating retriever, predictor and data-store terms.

title: LLMs Will Always Hallucinate, and We Need to Live With This
relevance: Undecidability-based argument that every LLM pipeline stage, including retrieval, has non-zero hallucination probability.

title: On the Optimal Memorization Capacity of Transformers
relevance: Shows near-optimal Otilde(sqrt N)-parameter memorization by transformers; parameter-count (not bit) capacity theory.

title: Softmax is not Enough (for Sharp Size Generalisation)
relevance: Proves softmax attention must disperse to Theta(1/n) with bounded logits; formal reason long contexts dilute evidence.

title: On the Limits of Language Generation: Trade-Offs Between Hallucination and Mode Collapse
relevance: Proves consistency plus breadth is impossible for next-token predictors without negative examples; hallucination vs mode-collapse trade-off.

title: Mind the Gap: Examining the Self-Improvement Capabilities of Large Language Models
relevance: Formalizes generation-verification gap governing self-improvement; theory of verification.

title: Understanding Factual Recall in Transformers via Associative Memories
relevance: Proves linear-in-parameters storage and a data-processing-inequality lower bound losing the tail beyond B/log M facts; key capacity theorem.

title: Scalable-Softmax Is Superior for Attention
relevance: Shows softmax attention fades as context grows and proposes log-n scaling; formal-empirical attention dilution.

title: On the Emergence of Position Bias in Transformers
relevance: Graph-theoretic proof that causal masks bias attention to early positions; theory of position bias.

title: NoLiMa: Long-Context Evaluation Beyond Literal Matching
relevance: NoLiMa shows large long-context degradation without literal matches; supports small reranked contexts.

title: Hallucinations are inevitable but can be made statistically negligible
relevance: Proves hallucination probability can be made negligible despite diagonal inevitability; probabilistic counterpoint.

title: Taming Knowledge Conflicts in Language Models
relevance: Finds superposition of context and memory in attention heads under knowledge conflict; mechanism of conflicts.

title: How do language models learn facts? Dynamics, curricula and hallucinations
relevance: Shows hallucinations emerge with knowledge and fine-tuning new facts corrupts memories; argues against fine-tuning facts in.

title: (Im)possibility of Automated Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
relevance: Proves hallucination detection equals language identification in the limit and becomes possible with negative examples; supports negative-labelled golden sets.

title: How much do language models memorize?
relevance: Estimates ~3.6 bits per parameter memorization capacity; independent bound on parametric memory.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation as Noisy In-Context Learning: A Unified Theory and Risk Bounds
relevance: Finite-sample RAG risk bounds as noisy ICL with a bias ceiling and optimal number of retrieved examples; supports small top-k.

title: On the Fundamental Impossibility of Hallucination Control in Large Language Models
relevance: Impossibility theorem for hallucination control via aggregation of component reports; low-confidence preprint.

title: Understanding and Mitigating Numerical Sources of Nondeterminism in LLM Inference
relevance: Traces greedy-decoding nondeterminism to floating-point non-associativity across GPU count, type and batch size; supports freezing extractions.

title: Hallucination as a Computational Boundary: A Hierarchy of Inevitability and the Oracle Escape
relevance: Claims RAG as oracle machine escapes inevitability hierarchy; low-confidence preprint.

title: Revisiting RAG Ensemble: A Theoretical and Mechanistic Analysis of Multi-RAG System Collaboration
relevance: Information-entropy analysis of ensembling multiple RAG systems.

title: On the Theoretical Limitations of Embedding-Based Retrieval
relevance: Sign-rank bound on top-k subsets realizable by single-vector embeddings; limit of the retrieval step itself.

title: Why Language Models Hallucinate
relevance: Reduces hallucination to IIV binary classification, bounds error by singleton rate, and proves binary grading never rewards abstention (incl. RAG); justifies abstention-aware golden-set scoring.

title: The Illusion of Diminishing Returns: Measuring Long Horizon Execution in LLMs
relevance: Gives horizon formula H_s=ln s/ln p and self-conditioning evidence; compounding error in long-horizon execution.

title: Hallucination is Inevitable for LLMs with the Open World Assumption
relevance: Argues hallucination is inevitable under open-world assumption; low-confidence preprint.

title: A Theory of Time-Sensitive Language Generation: Sparse Hallucination Beats Mode Collapse
relevance: Shows timely generation needs a vanishing hallucination rate; recent learning-in-the-limit result.

title: Don't Pick a Winner: Knowledge Conflicts Need a Prior, Not a Rule
relevance: Decision-theoretic proof that fixed knowledge-conflict rules are dominated and a context-reliability prior is required; supports validity/authority metadata.

title: Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference
relevance: Explains temperature-0 nondeterminism as lack of batch invariance in reduction kernels and shows batch-invariant kernels give identical outputs; supports freezing extractions.

title: Why language models hallucinate
relevance: Vendor summary of Kalai et al. with SimpleQA abstention/accuracy/error numbers (page returned 403; numbers via search snippet).

title: Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance
relevance: Shows across 18 models that performance degrades with input length and distractors; empirical support for small contexts.

title: Batch Invariance (vLLM documentation)
relevance: Documents vLLM's beta batch-invariant mode, its hardware/model limits and performance cost.

title: Reproducibility (PyTorch notes)
relevance: States reproducibility is not guaranteed across releases, commits or platforms; bounds what deterministic inference can promise.

title: What Every Computer Scientist Should Know About Floating-Point Arithmetic
relevance: Standard reference for rounding error bounds and order-dependence of floating-point sums; formal basis of inference nondeterminism.

title: The Accuracy of Floating Point Summation
relevance: Source of naive vs pairwise summation error bounds (cited via the Wikipedia summary; original not read).

title: Pairwise summation
relevance: States O(eps n) vs O(eps log n) summation error bounds showing results depend on reduction tree.

title: The Population Frequencies of Species and the Estimation of Population Parameters
relevance: Origin of the Good-Turing missing-mass estimator underlying the monofact/singleton hallucination bounds (bibliographic record and summary read, not full text).
